      operationId: get-dashboards
      parameters:
        - description: The page of results to return.
          in: query
          name: page
          required: false

            default: 1
            minimum: 1

        - description: The number of results to return per page.

          required: false

            default: 20

          in: query

          required: false
          schema:
            type: string
        - description: A tag ID to include. Accepts a single tag ID or multiple tag IDs. When multiple are specified, library items matching any of the tag IDs are included.
          in: query
          name: tags
          required: false
          schema:
            default: []
            description: Tag IDs associated with this dashboard.
            items:
              maxLength: 250
              type: string
            maxItems: 100
            type: array
        - description: A tag ID to exclude. Accepts a single tag ID or multiple tag IDs. When multiple are specified, library items matching any of the tag IDs are excluded.
          in: query
          name: excluded_tags
          required: false
          schema:
            default: []
            description: Tag IDs associated with this dashboard.
            items:
              maxLength: 250
              type: string
            maxItems: 100
            type: array
        - description: A tag name to include. Accepts a single tag name or multiple tag names. When multiple are specified, library items matching any of the tag names are included. If the same name is shared by multiple tags, items matching any of those tags are included.
          in: query
          name: tag_names
          required: false
          schema:
            items:
              type: string
            maxItems: 100
            type: array

The dashboard and the alert rule both exist, and Kibana accepted both. I haven't opened the dashboard in the UI. I also haven't checked that the rule runs cleanly or what it finds.

**Data view fields:** The `kibana_sample_data_logs` data view holds web access logs. The main fields are:
- `timestamp`
- `clientip`
- `bytes`
- `response`, a text field with a `.keyword` sub-field that supports aggregation
- `extension`
- `request`, `url` and `referer`
- `host`
- `machine.os`
- `agent`
- `geo.src`, `geo.dest` and `geo.coordinates`
- `memory` and `phpmemory`
- `tags`

**Dashboard:** "EFF-5f1fe843 Web logs overview" (id `02b7f889-f5bd-467b-b99e-0d5d054cbb3c`) defaults to the last 7 days and has five panels:
- Total requests
- Average bytes
- Unique clients
- Requests over time
- Requests by response code

**Rule:** "EFF-5f1fe843 5xx spike" (id `7ee9645a-8e74-43b7-b1fe-5dbfbd095769`) is an Elasticsearch query rule. It runs every minute over a 5-minute window and fires when the count of documents matching `response.keyword` ~ `5[0-9][0-9]` is above 10. It has no actions attached, so it will fire but won't send notifications until you add a connector.
